unit.title: Hay (there is/are)
unit.subtitle: Saying what exists and where things are

grammar.title: One tiny word for “there is” and “there are”
grammar.intro: Spanish uses a single word — hay — for both there is and there are. It never changes: hay un libro (there is a book), hay dos libros (there are two books). Pair it with a few prepositions of place and you can describe any room.

sections.heading: hay = there is / there are
sections.body: Hay is invariable — one word for singular and plural. Use it with un/una, unos/unas, a number, or a bare plural:

ex.en: There is a book on the table.
There are two chairs in the kitchen.

sections.heading: Prepositions of place
sections.body: These little words tell you where something is. Note that several end in de:

ex.es: Hay un gato debajo de la silla.
ex.en: There is a cat under the chair.
The dog is between the tables.

sections.heading: hay vs está / están
sections.body: Use hay to say something exists (usually with un/una/a number). Use está / están for the location of a specific, known thing:

ex.en: There is a book on the table.
The book is on the table.

takeaways: hay = there is AND there are — one word, it never changes.
Use hay with un/una, unos/unas, numbers, or bare plurals — never “hay son”.
“under / next to / on top of” often carry de: debajo de, al lado de.
hay = it exists; está/están = where a known thing is located.

mistakes.why: It is spelled hay (h + ay), not “ay” or “hax”.
hay already means “there are” — don’t add son.

mistakes.w: El gato está debajo la mesa.
mistakes.r: El gato está debajo de la mesa.
mistakes.why: debajo needs de: debajo de la mesa.

exercises.prompt_en: There are two cats in the house.

exercises.prompt: Build: “There is a book on the table.”
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Hay + un libro + sobre la mesa.
exercises.no: “Hay un libro sobre la mesa.” — hay, then the place.

exercises.prompt: Hay un gato debajo ___ la silla.
exercises.prompt_en: There is a cat under the chair.
exercises.hint: debajo ___ la silla — the little linking word.
exercises.no: debajo needs “de”: debajo de la silla.

exercises.prompt: Match each preposition to its meaning.

exercises.prompt_en: The book is on the table. (a specific, known book)
exercises.no: For a specific, known book’s location use “está”, not hay.

exercises.tts: Hay una silla al lado de la mesa.
accepted: hay una silla al lado de la mesa
exercises.translation: There is a chair next to the table.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Hay una silla al lado de la mesa.”
exercises.no: It was: “Hay una silla al lado de la mesa.” (There is a chair next to the table.)

exercises.scenario: A friend asks about your new kitchen 🍽️

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.en: What is there in the kitchen?

options.text: Hay una mesa y dos sillas.

exercises.no: The natural reply is “Hay una mesa y dos sillas.” (There is a table and two chairs.)
